LESSON: SELECTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.3: Selective Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Selective Listening, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 5 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it good to listen keenly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to audio recordings on items found in school and articulate target sounds and words correctly,

2. collaborate with peers to identify common colours,

3. chant a singing game involving different colours,

4. work jointly to describe classroom objects based on colour,

5. participate in conversations to describe classroom items in groups.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to audio recordings on items found in school and articulate target sounds and words correctly,
2. collaborate with peers to identify common colours,
3. chant a singing game involving different colours,
4. work jointly to describe classroom objects based on colour,
5. participate in conversations to describe classroom items in groups.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Selective Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with digital content when listening to audio recordings on items

found in school and articulate target sounds and words correctly.

• Creativity and imagination: This is promoted as the learner embraces ideas that ignite creativity when chanting a singing

game involving different colours.

Values:
Respect: This is enhanced as the learner appreciates diverse opinions from peers while participating in conversations to describe

classroom items.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental awareness: This is addressed as the learner discusses various classroom items and rooms in the schools

environment.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of colour with similar concepts as taught in Creative Arts.
